boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named destinations along South Orange Village corridors near Seton Hall, with one documented reason to stop at each.

cards.title: South Orange Performing Arts Center
cards.subtitle: One SOPAC Way, beside South Orange Avenue
cards.notes: Check SOPAC’s current calendar, then plan around a listed performance, screening, rehearsal, or community event.
cards.short_summary: A downtown nonprofit venue with a current public performance calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: SOPAC lists current performances and identifies its location as One SOPAC Way in South Orange Village.
cards.access_notes: Ticket requirements vary by event; consult the event listing before going.

cards.title: South Orange Station
cards.subtitle: Sloan Street corridor, between South Orange Avenue and First Street
cards.notes: Use the station as a rail-travel reference point; NJ TRANSIT lists Morris & Essex service and bike racks.
cards.short_summary: A named NJ TRANSIT station on the Sloan Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: NJ TRANSIT locates South Orange Station at 19 Sloan Street and lists Morris & Essex rail service and bike racks.
cards.access_notes: NJ TRANSIT lists weekday ticket-office hours; verify schedules and service alerts before travel.

cards.title: South Orange Public Library
cards.subtitle: South Orange Avenue corridor, near Scotland Road
cards.notes: Use the library’s official calendar or catalog before you go, and bring a valid library card if borrowing materials.
cards.short_summary: A named public-library stop in the Village center.
cards.evidence_claim: South Orange Village’s historic walking-tour guide identifies the Connett Library on South Orange Avenue near Village Hall.
cards.access_notes: Library services and program access can vary; verify current details with the library.

cards.title: South Orange Village Hall
cards.subtitle: South Orange Avenue corridor at Scotland Road
cards.notes: Pause outside to see a civic landmark, then use the Village site for public-meeting and service information.
cards.short_summary: A 1894 Village civic landmark on South Orange Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: South Orange Village states that Village Hall was built in 1894 and gives its municipal address as 76 South Orange Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Public access depends on municipal office hours and meetings.

cards.title: The Stone House
cards.subtitle: South Orange Avenue corridor near Grove Road
cards.notes: View this historic exterior from public space and pair it with the Village’s online history for context.
cards.short_summary: A documented circa-1680 house along South Orange Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: South Orange Village identifies the Stone House, near Grove Road on South Orange Avenue, as the Village’s oldest house and dates it to about 1680.
cards.access_notes: View from public areas only; this is not presented as a public interior attraction.

cards.title: Memorial Flagpole
cards.subtitle: South Orange Avenue corridor at Irvington Avenue
cards.notes: Make this a brief outdoor landmark stop while following the Village’s historic walking-tour route through downtown.
cards.short_summary: A named memorial landmark at the South Orange–Irvington intersection.
cards.evidence_claim: South Orange Village’s historic walking-tour guide places the Memorial Flagpole on the island at South Orange Avenue and Irvington Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public landmark; observe from sidewalks and follow traffic signals.

cards.title: The Baird Community Center
cards.subtitle: Mead Street corridor, one block off South Orange Avenue
cards.notes: Check the recreation calendar, then use the building’s listed art rooms, courts, meeting rooms, or program spaces as available.
cards.short_summary: A Village recreation facility with arts, sports, and meeting amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: South Orange Village lists The Baird at 5 Mead Street and identifies art classrooms, a basketball court, internet, meeting rooms, recreation programming, and tennis courts.
cards.source_title: South Orange Village: The Baird Community Center
cards.access_notes: Listed operating hours vary by day; individual programs and rooms may have separate access rules.

cards.title: Pierro Gallery
cards.subtitle: Mead Street corridor at the Baird Community Center
cards.notes: Look up the current exhibition before visiting, then spend time with the displayed visual art at this Village facility.
cards.short_summary: A municipal gallery presenting exhibitions by established and emerging artists.
cards.evidence_claim: The Village identifies Pierro Gallery at 5 Mead Street and says it presents diverse established and emerging visual artists through several exhibitions annually.
cards.access_notes: The Village describes the gallery as free and open to all; verify exhibition dates before visiting.

cards.title: Guanatico's Restaurant
cards.subtitle: Irvington Avenue corridor in Seton Village
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s official ordering or contact page to confirm the current menu and pickup or dining options.
cards.short_summary: A named Seton Village restaurant on the Irvington Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Village’s business directory lists Guanatico's Restaurant at 261-A Irvington Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Food purchase is required for dining; verify current service details directly with the business.

cards.title: Funky Fun Art
cards.subtitle: Irvington Avenue corridor in Seton Village
cards.notes: Check the studio’s current class or activity information before visiting, especially if you want to join a scheduled session.
cards.short_summary: A named art activity business on Irvington Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Village’s business directory lists Funky Fun Art at 204 Irvington Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Classes or activities may require advance registration or payment; confirm directly with the business.

warnings: Coordinates and direct map URLs were not independently verified, so they are omitted.
